officialOrganizations.name: Beltrami County/City of Bemidji
officialOrganizations.description: Geographic Information System (GIS) Beltrami County and the City of Bemidji formed a partnership for GIS software and online services in 2017. This GIS partnership provides support for all of Beltrami County's and the City Of Bemidji’s mapping needs. The GIS Departments at the county and the city develop online maps and applications as well as collect, manage and maintain many layers related to addressing, infrastructure, land use and more for their respective organizations. Our Mission Through this partnership, it is our mission to provide support through GIS to citizens and all departments so all decisions can be data-driven and completed with the most current, accurate and complete geospatial data available. We also strive to provide spatial information in a readily available and easy to use format.

officialOrganizations.name: Douglas County MN Survey & GIS
officialOrganizations.description: Welcome to the Douglas County MN GIS Home Page To view our applications, click on the icon above the description of the map you'd like to view. What is GIS? Geographic Information Systems or GIS has the ability to give tabular data and positional quality on a map or a computer screen. This is all done via a system of hardware, software, and geographic data. The mission of the Geographic Information System (GIS) Office is to provide geographically based information to citizens, other governmental units, and County staff, leading to better decision-making. We are continually improving this site and we plan on having the Maps and Apps that you are looking for. Send suggestions to Douglas County Survey . Additional Resources 2018 Douglas County City Map 2018 Douglas County Map 2015 Douglas County City Map 2015 Douglas County Map Open Data Portal Geospatial Data Request Plat Search Public Works Survey & GIS Internal Users Log on to the Douglas County GIS Portal If you encounter problems with this website please contact: Douglas County GIS Help Desk

officialOrganizations.name: Lake Superior Reserve
officialOrganizations.description: The Lake Superior National Estuarine Research Reserve, the most recent addition to the National Estuarine Reserve System, is one of 28 areas across the country designated for long-term research on coastal resources and the human populations those resources support. The Lake Superior NERR is located along a river-to-lake gradient at the confluence of the St. Louis River and Lake Superior, the largest and most pristine of the Great Lakes.The Superior-Duluth harbor is one of the largest ports in the U.S. The Reserve works in partnership to improve the understanding of Lake Superior freshwater estuaries and coastal resources and to address the issues affecting them through an integrated program of research, education, outreach, and stewardship. The Reserve is comprised exclusively of public lands and waters and contains ~16,000 acres of repesentative terrestrial and aquatic habitats, including riparian and riverine habitat; riverine islands; emergent freshwater marshes, interdunal wetlands and scrub swamp; aspen, dry and hardwood forests; and open sand beach and dunes. The Lake Superior Reserve land-owner partners are Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources, City of Superior, Douglas County and the University of Wisconsin. Several other partnering agencies, from both Minnesota and Wisconsin, and the Fond du Lac Band of the Lake Superior Chippewa also sit on our Reserve Advisory Board.

officialOrganizations.name: Town of Thomson, MN
officialOrganizations.description: Thomson Township is located in the northeast corner of Carlton County approximately 15 miles southwest of Duluth, Minnesota. With a population of 5,003, Thomson Township provides a small town atmosphere for its residents. Thomson Township is close to many area attractions in the Duluth, MN - Superior, WI area. One highlight would be in the southeastern corner of our township, you can find Jay Cooke State Park and the Munger Trail. Our Township also has a prime location for new businesses along Interstate 35 in the newly zoned Highway Commercial area. With our close proximity to the Spirit Mountain Recreation Area (12 miles NE) and less than 5 miles from Cloquet, our Highway Commercial area would be an excellent location for long-term business ventures due to direct freeway access and visibility.

officialOrganizations.name: POLK COUNTY LAND ASSET MANAGEMENT
officialOrganizations.description: The County of Polk is located in the northwest region of the State of Wisconsin, about 50 miles northeast of St. Paul, Minnesota and encompasses an area of 956 square miles. The County has 2 Cities, 24 Towns, and 12 Villages. The county seat is located in the central part of Polk County in the Village of Balsam Lake. We view location assets as being critically important to the welfare, health, and safety of Polk County citizens. A strategic location asset management system that delivers location based information improves effective decision making.

officialOrganizations.name: Wilkin County
officialOrganizations.description: Welcome to Wilkin County's GIS Hub Wilkin County has expanded access to its collection of public geographic information systems data, which can be used by the public and businesses for a variety of needs. This site provides county maps, apps and other resources in one single location. If you are unable to find information important to you, check out the County Webpage , or contact the Site Administrator . Your feedback is important to the development of the county's available resources. Advances in Wilkin County's GIS technology benefit its departments, private entities, government organizations, and citizens. We hope you find the value in the improved access to public information. The new Open Data site provides enhanced options for accessing, exploring and downloading unique county datasets. A compatible mapping program is necessary to read spatial data. Data may also be downloaded in spreadsheet format. The Interactive Mapping and Mobile Mapping apps can be used to identify and locate land parcels within the county. Maps are for reference purposes only and may not be construed or used as a legal description. The physical location is approximate and does not replace survey information. Disclaimer Notice Wilkin County Courthouse 300 5th St S Breckenridge, MN 56520 © 2017 Wilkin County, Minnesota. Site development by Pro-West & Associates, Inc.

officialOrganizations.name: City of Minnetonka
officialOrganizations.description: Located in Hennepin County just eight miles west of Minneapolis, Minnetonka is a fully developed suburban community of just under 50,000 residents. Minnetonka is proud of its reputation as a city that preserves its natural resources—residents can enjoy 49 community parks, more than 81 miles of maintained sidewalks and trails and more than 1,000 acres of public open space, as well as natural scenery that includes mature trees, wetlands and prairies. While Minnetonka shares its name with the very popular Lake Minnetonka, the city of Minnetonka includes only one small bay of the lake – Gray’s Bay, which forms the headwaters of Minnehaha Creek.

officialOrganizations.name: Washington County, MN
officialOrganizations.description: Washington County was created October 27, 1849, in the Territory of Minnesota. Minnesota was admitted to the United States as the 32nd state on May 11, 1858. As one of Minnesota's original nine counties, Washington County is on the eastern edge of the Twin Cities Metropolitan area, composed of 423 square miles of land, and possessing a distinct set of landscapes and resources. It runs more than 40 miles in length, and encompasses 468 lakes of 10 acres or more in area. The county seat is in Stillwater, Minnesota, along the scenic St. Croix River.

officialOrganizations.description: Lyon County operates a Geographic Information System (GIS) to provide current and accurate geospatial (map) information to County departments, the general public and other entities. We seek to ensure that Lyon County residents and decision makers have access to geographic information that is complete, timely, accurate, and reliable. We promote the use of GIS and related technologies to more effectively and efficiently address problems, develop plans, and manage the natural, cultural, economic, and infrastructure resources of the county. Lyon County is implementing GIS to streamline county operations and to make County data and records available to the citizens of Lyon County.

officialOrganizations.name: Rice County, MN
officialOrganizations.description: General Information Rice County is located in Southern Minnesota just 30 miles south of the Minneapolis and St. Paul metropolitan area. The County encompasses an area of 496 square miles and contains 7 cities and 14 townships. The two largest cities in Rice County are Faribault with a population of 22,798, and Northfield with a population of 18,801. Rice County has a total population of 63,034 which is the State's 13th most populous county. Rice County was organized on March 5, 1853, and is governed by the general laws of the State of Minnesota. The cities of Faribault and Northfield comprise slightly less than three quarters of the County's total taxable value. Governmental Organization & Services The Rice County Board of Commissioners consists of five commissioners elected from five districts in the County. All commissioners serve overlapping four-year terms of office. Each member of the board serves on various committees. The Board appoints the County Administrator who is the chief executive officer of the County. The Administrator is responsible for the administration of Board policy and for the management of the various County departments. The County's functions and employees are divided among 16 departments. Four of these departments - Attorney, Auditor/Treasurer, Recorder and Sheriff - are headed by members who are elected to office. The remaining department heads are appointed by the County Board. The County provides a full range of services. These services include: health and social services; tax assessment and collection; judicial, law enforcement and jail services; the construction and maintenance of highways and infrastructure; recreational facilities, planning and zoning; and general administrative services. The General Fund budget of Rice County is approximately $21 million and the total budget is $49 million. The County has approximately 330 full-time equivalent employees. Interstate Highway 35 bisects Rice County from north to south. Minnesota State Highways 99, 60, 246, and 21 traverse the County. Air transportation is available through the Faribault Municipal Airport.
